speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I will share the preliminary findings for each incident.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, the North-South Line (NSL) incident on 7 February.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: At around 5.15 am, an engineering vehicle broke down at a railway crossing in Bishan Depot after routine maintenance works.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This engineering vehicle comprises three wagons, which are used for carrying equipment and materials for maintenance works and two locomotives, which are used for moving the wagons along the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) tracks.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As trains departing Bishan Depot for the mainline need to pass through this railway crossing, SMRT was unable to launch trains from Bishan Depot.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To allow operations to resume, SMRT attempted to move the stalled engineering vehicle using a rescue train.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When the rescue train started moving the stalled vehicle, SMRT discovered that some of the wheels of two of the wagons had come off the rails.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To ensure that commuters using the NSL could still continue on their journeys, SMRT redirected some trains from the East-West Line (EWL) to the NSL.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This allowed train services to continue operating throughout the day on both lines, but with a longer interval between trains during peak hours.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT also activated free regular and free bridging buses along the busiest stretch of the NSL between Woodlands and Bishan stations, to provide commuters with an alternative travel option.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As there were fewer trains during peak periods, commuters experienced longer waiting times at the stations, but their travel times were largely unaffected once they boarded the train.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Meanwhile, SMRT had continued with their recovery efforts to move the stalled engineering vehicle.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Due to the tight space around the depot tracks, SMRT was unable to use heavy lifting cranes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It had to use hydraulic equipment to slowly and safely shift the stalled vehicle onto another track.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The stalled vehicle was cleared off the railway crossing by around 5.30 pm.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Next, the North East Line (NEL) incident on 10 February.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: At around 6.08 am, a signalling fault occurred near Buangkok station.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This prevented the NEL trains from being controlled automatically.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a result, while trains could still travel along the NEL, they had to be controlled manually and travel at slower speeds to ensure safety.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This led to reduced frequency of service and additional travel time for commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In response to this decrease in service capacity, SBS Transit (SBST) activated free regular and bridging buses along the NEL between Punggol Coast and Dhoby Ghaut stations at 6.55 am to provide commuters with an alternative travel option.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Preliminary investigations indicate that the signalling fault was caused by a malfunctioning electronic card in the signalling system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There were no prior signs during the maintenance checks which showed that this card would malfunction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SBST replaced the malfunctioning electronic card, and was able to restore the signalling system’s operations at around 8.00 am, following which normal train service was progressively restored.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The faulty electronic card has been sent to the system manufacturer for further examination, to identify the root cause of the malfunction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Third, the Circle Line (CCL) incident on 11 February.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In LTA’s earlier statement on 13 February 2025, it noted that a power trip had occurred arising from a signalling fault.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Further investigations show that there was no power trip and that the incident was due to a signalling fault.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Based on LTA’s latest findings, at around 8.15 am, a signalling fault caused a temporary loss of communications between a CCL train and the trackside signalling equipment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The other trains near the incident train will also come to a stop to ensure safety for commuters, by keeping the trains at a safe distance from one another until communications can be fully restored.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Due to this signalling fault, 17 trains between Paya Lebar and Marymount stations were temporarily halted for safety.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT promptly withdrew the incident train from the mainline and after doing the necessary safety checks, train movement resumed progressively from 8.20 am, five minutes after the signalling fault had occurred.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, when train operations were being restored, SMRT noticed that the Central Automatic Train Supervision (CATS) System, which manages the movement of trains, became less responsive.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a result, it took longer than usual to resume normal train operations, even though trains had started moving on the CCL.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The delay in resumption of normal train operations led to longer wait times and travel durations for some CCL commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We had experienced a similar issue with the CATS system in September 2024.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: After that incident, LTA and SMRT worked with the system manufacturer Alstom to develop a software patch to address the issue.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The patch went through extensive testing and was ready for deployment on 15 February.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Unfortunately, the incident happened a few days before the deployment date.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT and Alstom have since successfully deployed the software patch.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Not just for LTA, but also for our tripartite partners in the One Transport Family.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: While we cannot completely prevent incidents from happening in a rail system of this size and complexity, we certainly will do our best together with the operators and our workers to maintain a high level of safety, reliability and resilience, and to minimise the impact to commuters when an incident occurs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Through this approach, we have achieved our one million mean kilometres between failure (MKBF) target consistently since 2019, which puts our overall system among the best performing metros in the world.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Rail safety, reliability and resilience are key priorities for LTA and our tripartite partners.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will continue to work close together on this front to identify areas for improvement, adopt new technologies for more effective maintenance and operations, and invest in the skills of our workers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second question, during the debate after the six-day breakdown of the EWL after Jurong East station in September 2024, the Minister rejected my call for the convening of a Committee of Inquiry.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Now that we have three more MRT disruptions in less than a week, I would like to ask the Minister whether he would now call for a Committee of Inquiry this time?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, LTA is looking into the root causes for the three incidents that had happened in February.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I have explained in my main reply what we think are some of the preliminary findings, why these three incidents happened on three separate lines.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope Mr Leong would agree with me that these three incidents are unrelated to one another and also the nature would be quite different from what happened to the EWL disruption in September last year.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have not completed our investigations for the EWL incident or for these three incidents.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we will certainly do our best to identify what are the learning points and then, to make sure that we share this with all the operators – not just in this case SMRT for the EWL, Circle Line and NSL, and SBST for the NEL, but we also want to encourage them to share these learning points in the whole One Transport Family so that everyone can benefit and do better.
Mr Leong is right that we should go beyond hardware because it is a review of the whole system of operations and maintenance.
And we have certainly been looking at these issues as well and we will continue to do so.

I also want to thank Mr Leong for highlighting the importance of staff morale for our engineering and technical teams, because that is a very important part of ensuring smooth operations and good maintenance.

And that is why we always emphasise that we want to continue to work closely together as tripartite partners to make sure that we uphold high standards of safety, reliability and resilience for our commuters.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And following this incident, will LTA look into the maintenance regime for the maintenance vehicles, because, obviously, it may impact on the operations of our passenger trains?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Relating to that, will SMRT also look at better service recovery of stalled engineering vehicles along the tracks?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Besides the engineering vehicle issue, I would also like to ask the Minister, beyond bridging bus services during a breakdown, how can operators and LTA improve the public communication process at affected stations with commuters during train disruptions?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For example, can operators push out information on regular bus services operating near the affected stations to alleviate the demand on the bridging bus services?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The first one, on the engineering vehicle, the maintenance.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are not the same as MRT trains.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I have explained, the two locomotives, three wagons and the nature of how they operate will also be quite different from MRT trains.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we do not subject them to the exact same maintenance regime as a normal MRT train because they are different vehicles.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we do have a maintenance regime in place for the engineering vehicles as well.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This time round, we are still checking what happened.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I do not want to prematurely jump to any conclusions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will let LTA finish their investigations to understand what the root causes are and why this engineering vehicle broke down.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To Mr Tan's second question on the service recovery, I do want to be fair to SMRT.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They tried their very best to move the train as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it became a very labour-intensive and quite time-consuming process of having to use hydraulic equipment to try and move this very heavy engineering vehicle.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It took them a long time to do so.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They only managed to do so at about 5.00-plus pm, as I have explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I do want to be fair to SMRT.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They were trying their very best to move the vehicle as quickly as possible, while, of course, adhering to the necessary safety protocols.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Tan's third question, Mr Speaker, is on the response during an incident.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think this is an area where we will continue, as part of the learning, to see how we can finetune our communications with commuters and to see what we can do to improve.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: During peak hours, I think Mr Tan will agree with me that, given the large number of commuters, even on a normal day it is quite crowded.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And when there is a delay or when there is a longer headway for the trains, it will cause the crowd to build up.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT and SBS Transit, in these incidents, did their best to try and communicate with the affected commuters, not just those who are already in the system but even those who are not yet coming into the system, to advise them so that they can consider alternative transport arrangements, which could include bridging buses and regular buses travelling along that same route, but also to take alternative MRT lines.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is the other option for commuters to consider.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this is still a work in progress and I hope to share more during the Committee of Supply (COS) debates.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I declare that I am the Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I recently met with many of our rail workers serving the affected lines and they are proud public transport workers who bear their work with great purpose and a heavy responsibility to commuters and the community.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What will the Ministry do to further empower and uplift our rail workers to do their work more efficiently and effectively, given the complexity and age of the infrastructure?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And as I have replied to Mr Leong earlier, the staff morale of the teams would also be equally important.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I hope to share more during the COS debates.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I seek Ms Yeo's understanding that more details would be made available during the COS debates.
